## 2. Strategy
**engine-recompile** — Unity 2021+ with Android Build Support (IL2CPP arm64, Gradle).

The engine itself targets the destination: this is configuration + adaptation work, not a rewrite. Usually days, not weeks.

## 3. Phases
1. Install Android Build Support module in Unity Hub (SDK+NDK+JDK come bundled)
2. File → Build Settings → Android → Switch Platform
3. Player Settings: IL2CPP, ARM64 + (optional ARMv7), strip engine code
4. Remap input to New Input System touch bindings; add on-screen controls
5. UI: switch Canvas Scaler to Scale With Screen Size (portrait or ratio-matched)
6. Gradle build → .apk/.aab → test on device via adb
7. Store prep: target API level per current Play requirements, 16KB page size

## 4. Risks
- Native plugins (.dll) need Android .so equivalents or removal
- IL2CPP stripping can break reflection-heavy code (link.xml to preserve)
- Textures: switch to ASTC compression for GPU mem

## 5. QA matrix (a port that wasn't tested is a plan)
- [ ] installs via adb on real device (not just emulator)
- [ ] cold start < 5s on a mid-tier phone
- [ ] core loop 60fps (or honest degraded mode)
- [ ] touch input + back button correct
- [ ] save/load survives app kill
- [ ] network failure paths degrade gracefully
- [ ] 64-bit only (arm64-v8a) — Play requirement
- [ ] target API level current
- [ ] 16KB page-size alignment (new devices)
